question.problem: Suppose $A$ is a $5\times 5$ matrix and $det(A)=-31.$ The matrix $B$ is obtained from $A$ by applying the elementary row operation ${R}_{2}↔{R}_{4}$ (switching the second and the fourth rows). What is the value of $det(B)?$

current_example.problem: Suppose $A$ is a $3 \times 3$ matrix and $\det (A) = -16.$ The matrix $B$ is obtained from $A$ by applying the elementary row operation $R_1 \leftrightarrow R_2$ (switching the first and the second rows). What is the value of $\det(B)?$
current_example.worked_solution:
Since swapping any two rows changes the sign of the determinant to the opposite sign, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}det(B) & =-det(A) \\  & =-(-16) \\  & =16.\end{aligned}
$$
